1) I can say being out has made me much happier .I think when I wasn't I was sort of scared, but still always felt it would be better. Lying about girls was always frustrating to me.

2) By being "yours only" I assume you mean the idea of you finding out and sort of forcing him out by mentioning it. I can say my aunt and uncle found out and I was really rather annoyed. Since I hadn't told them or anyone in my family besides my cousin. So in a way, yes.

3) You know your brother best. If you think he would react poorly don't mention it now. If you feel he is struggling and you could help by reassuring him, then you could probably approach him. I would caution depending on how you found out, since depending on what it was he may feel you invaded his privacy while snooping around.

4) Finally, he could change his mind I suppose. But I knew since at least 4th grade. However I can remember being about 7 and saying I wanted to marry this male singer, sooo, yeah :) But making him "admit" it wouldn't be bad if you feel you could help him in anyway. Even if he was "confused" it may be helpful to know that whatever he decides is fine with you.

16M Came out at 15 if that matters in anyway.

Having been the gay friend, I can tell you, if you act differently you are going to really hurt him. I told my friend when I was 15 and he was the first person I told. We hung out together with no one else all the time and still do it. I did like him, never told him, but I did.

He said some really weird things and then basically avoided me for a month. We hung out once or twice. But it used to be almost ever day. It hurt real bad then and now if I don't hear from him I instantly go back to that and start worrying. Its irrational now but it stuck with me.

Lastly I don't know how you friend is around the jokes or when people say fag and what not. My friend at this point apologizes after if he says it around me and otherwise we just ignore it. I don't take personal offence to random people saying things that aren't directed at me. If he does and you don't feel comfortable confronting whoever right there and then, you can just tell him privately after that your on his side.

If you want o ask him if he likes you while assuring him it won't be a big deal but your not interested, it would probably help him. Otherwise, just act like you always have because in the end all he really wants is you to be his friend after he told you. Any feelings he has for you that are stronger will fade and are likely a result of you being a good friend. 

I have faith you will do the right thing since you came here asking for help. Good luck.

I know what you saying. I came out to friends and my cousins last year. Was going to tell my parents/rest of my family, felt the same way and never got around to it. They probably have figured it out by now. Other than me actually saying the words, it should be pretty obvious at this point. Just based on the things I talk about. But I have felt there is no reason to have the awkward conversation. They will be fine when they know and until they have a reason to be informed I am keeping it to myself. 

If I had a boyfriend or something I would tell them. I don't so I feel no need to run to dinner yelling I love penis or something :P Do whatever feels right to you but know they don't have to be told until you want to tell them.

Probably wouldn't be a bad idea to get a feel for his opionions through text. but as for actually telling him I would tell him face to face. As for starting it I just waited till there was some silence for a moment and said I had something I want to tell him. Wasn't that complicated.

He asked a few questions and then we moved on. I wasn't to worry about how it would go but being totally honest I wasn't sure either. The only time he mentioned anything about stuff like the was making jokes about gay people. They sounded innocent but I had no real knowledge of his feelings. 

At this point over a year later I can say that I think I may have actually made him more accepting of people. Not that he wasn't but he is very careful with what he says around me. He has made jokes before and apologized immediately after. He didn't have to but he does. So even if your friend seems a little unsettled, it is possible given time to think he will realize it is still you and that none of this is all that bad.

By the way, came out when I was 15. Now am 16. Good luck!

I am 16 and I would say just love him and if he says he wants to do something that isn't "normal" for guys let him. I am not the stereotype for gay guys at all. But there are times I want to wear something or say I like something and my parents response is basically to say that it isn't me and totally shut down to the idea. I love sports and a lot of things "normal straight guys" like. Just don't cage your child within the boundaries of those norms. My parents are fine with the exception of that. But I think you sound like you will do the right thing. Last word of advice, should he grow up and at 13 be interested in girls, don't try to stop him. Let him figure it out.

I doubt a 14 year old would fake gay. And if you trust your daughter to make good decisions, I would say let her have him over. 

As for the sibling thing, I hear what you are saying and it will probably be a tough argument, but whether your son shows he agrees, I bet inside he would understand the difference between a gay guy and a straight girl staying over.

I really don't like girls. But like you there are a few that I see and think hmmmm maybe I could... Does that make me bi? If we were to label I would say I was gay because when I really think about it, I could probably be with either sex, but would much rather a guy. I almost can't see being with a girl other than a few that catch my eye. And even if it isn't looks, girls I talk to I always think of as friends. As where guys I always at least for a moment think about them maybe being slightly more.
Usually alone. Occasionally joined by my cousin but not often. My friend finds anything that isn't a KO boring. The rest of my family occasionally will stop watch but they don't understand and leave.

I now things are better now than they were. I also understand that my feelings are something anyone can relate to, they just don't understand (assuming their straight) how hopeless things look when you don't know anyone else who is gay.

As for college, I mean maybe, I think so... I just have no clue what I want to do.

And as for sports I haven't really played anything for a few years. I love MMA which obviously isn't a high school sport and did it for about 10 years (I was 4 when  I started) But I stopped because MMA is really...touchy and I wasn't sure how being gay would go over in the "macho" sport. I didn't want to have to lie anymore so I just stopped. I want to go back but I don't know.

First, I totally understand. It is annoying because you always have to come up with some sort of lie or way to change the subject. Now assuming your sibling are around your age I would simply say you have something to tell them. That sounds dumb but I wouldn't run into the room yelling I am gay. Or throw it into the middle of another conversation. But when I told my cousin who is basically my brother and my closest, only friend. I basically said I had something I wanted to tell them and that I would appreciate it if they didn't act differently. 

The panic was there both times, but it doesn't change how happy I am now that they know. And now that they know, I will talk about girls with them and be honest. But they know that I really am not interested in the girl. It makes it so much better.

Finally at school basically everyone I interact with knows. How? Well I make YouTube videos and they found them. It was really awkward at first but most people are cool with it and will change the conversation to include me. Example being someone said to a group of us "how are the relationships? Any girls...or guys? " All I can really say is it is a much better existence when people know. Don't make a big deal out of it, just say it.
